seo.homeOgTitle: Your own ShareX server and file cloud
seo.homeOgDescription: Capture, upload and share from Windows, browse files in File Explorer and search them with AI on your own server.

desktop.title: A native Windows app
desktop.text: Capture a region across every monitor, annotate it, copy text with OCR or record a video or GIF. The link lands on your clipboard.

harbor.title: Your files in File Explorer

ai.title: AI search on your server

zipline.description: Compare Fileship and Zipline: both are self-hosted ShareX servers. Fileship adds a Windows app, File Explorer sync, AI search and zero-downtime updates, and imports your Zipline accounts, files and links.
zipline.intro: Zipline is a popular self-hosted ShareX server, and Fileship covers the same ground: uploads from ShareX and other tools, nested folders, short links, passwords, expiry and view limits. Fileship then adds the apps around it, so it feels like your own file cloud.
zipline.ahead: Zipline signs in with OAuth providers such as Discord, GitHub and Google as well as OpenID Connect, while Fileship supports OpenID Connect only. Zipline is MIT licensed; Fileship is AGPL-3.0.
zipline.migrate: Fileship imports a Zipline 3.7 or 4.x server export: accounts with their passwords, files with their names, link names, dates and views, nested folders and short links. Old /u/ links keep working once the domain points at Fileship.

xbackbone.description: Compare Fileship and XBackBone: both are self-hosted ShareX servers. Fileship adds folders, sharing limits, a Windows app, File Explorer sync and AI search, and imports your XBackBone users and files.
xbackbone.intro: XBackBone is a lightweight PHP file manager for ShareX. Fileship accepts the same uploads and adds nested folders, notes, short links, passwords, expiry and view limits, plus a Windows app and a browser extension.
xbackbone.ahead: XBackBone runs on plain PHP hosting without Docker, offers more storage backends and signs in with LDAP, which Fileship does not support.
xbackbone.migrate: Fileship imports an XBackBone 3 SQLite database with its storage folder: users with their email addresses, and files with their names, link names and dates. Users set a new password, because XBackBone hashes passwords with bcrypt.

chibisafe.description: Compare Fileship and Chibisafe: both are self-hosted file uploaders. Fileship adds nested folders, sharing limits, a Windows app, File Explorer sync and AI search, and imports your Chibisafe files, albums and snippets.
chibisafe.intro: Chibisafe is a self-hosted file uploader with albums and a browser extension. Fileship has the same, with nested folders instead of flat albums, and adds passwords, expiry and view limits, notes, a Windows app and AI search.
chibisafe.ahead: Chibisafe is MIT licensed and has a simpler setup with fewer moving parts.
chibisafe.migrate: Fileship imports a Chibisafe 6 SQLite database with its uploads folder: accounts, files with their names, link names and dates, albums as folders, short links and snippets as notes.

free.a: Yes. Fileship is open source under AGPL-3.0, and you run it on your own server.
